rules.quote: Include all dialogue
rules.specification: Completeness requires comparison with the source recording; the transcript alone cannot establish whether dialogue is missing.
rules.violation_condition: A transcript omits dialogue from the source recording.
when: The text is a transcript of video or audio.
rules.why: G-1: dialogue completeness is distinct from identifying the speakers.

covers.quote: If there is only one speaker, introduce them by name in the transcript.
You can then leave out their name with the dialogue, unless it is crucial to the content.

rules.quote: Include all dialogue and the speakers’ names.
rules.violation_condition: A transcript fails to identify its speakers by name, or fails to name its sole speaker at the beginning.
when: The text is a transcript.
With only one speaker, an initial introduction by name is sufficient.
Repeat a sole speaker’s name with the dialogue only when it is crucial to the content.
rules.why: G-2 and G-3: the single-speaker instructions are conditions and an exception to the speaker-identification check.

rules.quote: Write non-verbal information in square brackets.
rules.violation_condition: Non-verbal information in a transcript is not enclosed in square brackets.
when: The text is a transcript and includes non-verbal information.
rules.why: G-1: this is a distinct notation check for non-verbal information.

rules.quote: End the transcript with ‘End of transcript’.
rules.violation_condition: A transcript does not end with the words ‘End of transcript’.
when: The text is a transcript.
rules.why: G-4: ordinary prose following the example states a new rule.

covers.quote: Government agencies might use alternative spellings in video content for some overseas audiences.

rules.quote: Use Australian terms and spelling for an Australian audience, regardless of the accent or intention of the speaker.
rules.violation_condition: Captions or subtitles intended for an Australian audience use non-Australian terms or spelling merely to reproduce the speaker’s accent or intended spelling.
when: The text is captions or subtitles for an Australian audience.
Alternative spellings may be used in government video content for some overseas audiences.
rules.why: G-2 and G-3: the audience determines when the spelling and terminology check applies.

rules.quote: Keep captions and subtitles short: no more than 2 lines, with no more than 42 characters per line.
rules.violation_condition: A caption or subtitle has more than 2 lines, or a line contains more than 42 characters.
when: The text is a caption or subtitle block.
rules.why: G-1: the sentence defines one caption-length check with explicit line and character limits.

rules.quote: Make line breaks where there is a natural break in the sentence (for example, after a comma).
rules.specification: The manual gives a comma as an example but does not define all acceptable natural breaks.
rules.violation_condition: A caption or subtitle line break interrupts a syntactic unit rather than falling at a natural break in the sentence.
when: The text is captions or subtitles split across lines.
rules.why: G-1: placement of a line break is separate from the length limits.

rules.quote: give each speaker a separate line
rules.violation_condition: A caption or subtitle containing 2 speakers places both speakers’ dialogue on the same line.
when: A caption or subtitle block contains 2 speakers.
rules.why: G-1 and G-2: speaker separation is one check, conditional on there being 2 speakers.

rules.quote: start each line with a dash
rules.violation_condition: A speaker’s line in a caption or subtitle with 2 speakers does not start with a dash.
when: A caption or subtitle block contains 2 speakers.
rules.why: G-1: the missing speaker dash is distinct from failing to separate the speakers onto different lines.

rules.quote: Don’t use a full stop at the end of subtitles.
rules.violation_condition: A subtitle ends with a full stop.
when: The text is a subtitle.
An ellipsis indicating trailing or unfinished speech is not a terminal full stop.
rules.why: G-1: terminal full stops are a separate punctuation check from indicating unfinished speech.

rules.quote: Use an ellipsis to indicate the end of a sentence where speech trails off or where a sentence remains unfinished.
rules.violation_condition: A subtitle does not use an ellipsis to mark speech that trails off or a sentence that remains unfinished.
when: The subtitle represents speech that trails off or remains unfinished.
rules.why: G-2: trailing off and remaining unfinished are two triggers for the same ellipsis check.

covers.quote: dialogue that is not on the screen, such as a public announcement or dialogue from a television program.

rules.quote: Use italics for:
rules.violation_condition: A foreign word or phrase, or dialogue from an off-screen source, is not italicised in captions or subtitles.
when: The text is captions or subtitles.
The text is a foreign word or phrase, or dialogue from an off-screen source such as a public announcement or television program.
rules.why: G-2: both listed cases trigger the same missing-italics check.

rules.quote: Any video or audio content you publish must have:
rules.violation_condition: Published video or audio content lacks a written title or description.
when: Video or audio content is published.
This check concerns the written title and description, not the file’s metadata or file name.
rules.why: G-1: required descriptive text is distinct from the later checks on its wording; file properties are excluded.

rules.quote: has 70 characters or fewer so that search engines can find it
rules.violation_condition: The title of video or audio content contains more than 70 characters.
when: The text is the title of video or audio content.
rules.why: G-1: title length is a specific child check, not a second copy of the section heading.

rules.quote: includes keywords
rules.specification: The page does not identify required keywords or define how they should be selected. A checker needs the content’s subject and intended search terms.
rules.violation_condition: The title of video or audio content lacks relevant keywords.
when: The text is the title of video or audio content.
rules.why: G-1: keyword inclusion is distinct from title length and general descriptiveness.

rules.quote: is descriptive, telling users what the content is about.
rules.violation_condition: The title does not tell users what the video or audio content is about.
when: The text is the title of video or audio content.
rules.why: G-1: a title can satisfy the length and keyword checks without adequately describing the content.

rules.quote: Use the description to explain if the content is part of a series and tell people how they can subscribe.
rules.violation_condition: The description of content in a series does not explain its series membership or how people can subscribe.
when: The video or audio content is part of a series.
rules.why: G-2: series membership is the condition for the series-information check.

covers.quote: For interviews or ‘talking heads’, the usual style is to place the speaker’s name on the top line.

rules.quote: Place the speaker’s title and organisation on the second line.
rules.violation_condition: An interview or talking-head lower third does not put the speaker’s name on the top line and their title and organisation on the second line.
when: The text is a lower third for an interview or talking-head video.
rules.why: G-2: both lines form one ordering convention for the speaker-identification block.

rules.quote: be correct
rules.specification: Apply this to the accuracy of the written name, title and organisation. Verification requires an authoritative source.
rules.violation_condition: A lower third contains incorrect speaker-identification information.
when: The text is a lower third in a video.
rules.why: G-1: accuracy of the words is a separate check from the overlay’s visual properties.

rules.quote: be as short as possible
rules.specification: Interpret brevity as omitting unnecessary wording while retaining the information needed to identify the speaker; the manual gives no numerical limit.
rules.violation_condition: A lower third contains wording that can be removed without losing necessary speaker-identification information.
when: The text is a lower third in a video.
rules.why: G-1 and E-4: brevity is distinct from correctness, and its operational interpretation is made explicit.

anchor.quote: Include all dialogue
anchor.suffix: and the speakers’ names. If the

tags.specification: Completeness requires comparison with the source recording; the transcript alone cannot establish whether dialogue is missing.
tags.violation_condition: A transcript omits dialogue from the source recording.

when: The text is a transcript of video or audio.
rules.why: G-1: dialogue completeness is distinct from identifying the speakers.

anchor.quote: Include all dialogue and the speakers’ names.
anchor.suffix: If there is only one speaker, i

covers.quote: If there is only one speaker, introduce them by name in the transcript.
covers.suffix: You can then leave out their na

covers.prefix: them by name in the transcript.
covers.quote: You can then leave out their name with the dialogue, unless it is crucial to the content.

tags.violation_condition: A transcript fails to identify its speakers by name, or fails to name its sole speaker at the beginning.

when: The text is a transcript.
With only one speaker, an initial introduction by name is sufficient.
Repeat a sole speaker’s name with the dialogue only when it is crucial to the content.
rules.why: G-2 and G-3: the single-speaker instructions are conditions and an exception to the speaker-identification check.

anchor.quote: Write non-verbal information in square brackets.

examples.note: The requested examples field is not available in the response schema.

parts.quote: ‘… to get to the other side [laughing].’

tags.violation_condition: Non-verbal information in a transcript is not enclosed in square brackets.

when: The text is a transcript and includes non-verbal information.
rules.why: G-1: this is a distinct notation check for non-verbal information.

anchor.quote: End the transcript with ‘End of transcript’.

tags.violation_condition: A transcript does not end with the words ‘End of transcript’.

when: The text is a transcript.
rules.why: G-4: ordinary prose following the example states a new rule.

anchor.quote: Use Australian terms and spelling for an Australian audience, regardless of the accent or intention of the speaker.
anchor.suffix: Government agencies might use a

covers.prefix: nt or intention of the speaker.
covers.quote: Government agencies might use alternative spellings in video content for some overseas audiences.

tags.violation_condition: Captions or subtitles intended for an Australian audience use non-Australian terms or spelling merely to reproduce the speaker’s accent or intended spelling.

when: The text is captions or subtitles for an Australian audience.
Alternative spellings may be used in government video content for some overseas audiences.
rules.why: G-2 and G-3: the audience determines when the spelling and terminology check applies.
